fullName: RRB NTPC — Non-Technical Popular Categories (Graduate & Undergraduate)
overview: RRB NTPC recruits for non-technical Railway posts through separate graduate and undergraduate notifications. **The current CEN 06/2026 graduate table has four posts:** Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor, Goods Train Manager, Junior Accounts Assistant cum Typist and Senior Clerk cum Typist. **CEN 07/2026 undergraduate posts** are Commercial cum Ticket Clerk, Accounts Clerk cum Typist, Junior Clerk cum Typist and Trains Clerk. The common CBT subjects are Mathematics, Reasoning and General Awareness. Selection uses CBT 1, CBT 2, a qualifying typing test for the notified typist posts, document verification and the prescribed medical examination. There is no interview. Station Master and Traffic Assistant appeared in other NTPC recruitments and should not be assumed to be advertised in the current graduate CEN.

stages.name: CBT 1 — First Stage (screening)
stages.notes: One 90-minute block (120 minutes for PwBD candidates with scribe/eligibility) — no sectional timing, so you choose the order. Qualifying percentages used in the last cycle: **UR/EWS 40%, OBC-NCL and SC 30%, ST 25%**. Marks are normalised across shifts. CBT 1 marks do **not** carry into the final merit.

selectionProcess: **Current CEN 06/2026 and 07/2026: CBT 1 → CBT 2 → qualifying typing test for the notified typist posts → document verification → medical examination.** Match the post-specific stages and medical standard in the detailed CEN. Station Master/Traffic Assistant aptitude rules from other NTPC cycles should not be applied to this graduate four-post table.
normalization: RRB conducts CBT 1 and CBT 2 across many days and shifts with different question papers, so scores are **normalised across shifts** before results are declared: a statistical adjustment makes sure a tougher paper doesn't hurt you and an easier one doesn't help you. In practice: (1) never compare raw scores with friends in other shifts; (2) attempt according to the paper you actually get, not the one you expected; (3) a raw score slightly below the cut-off you've heard about is not the end — only the normalised score is compared.

faqs.q: Is there negative marking in RRB NTPC?
faqs.a: One-third mark is deducted for a wrong answer in CBT 1 and CBT 2; unattempted questions score zero. Follow the current CEN for the qualifying typing test. Other cycles’ CBAT rules do not determine the current four-post graduate recruitment.

faqs.q: What is the CBT 1 and CBT 2 pattern?
faqs.a: **CBT 1:** 100 questions in 90 minutes — Mathematics 30, Reasoning 30, General Awareness 40. **CBT 2:** 120 questions in 90 minutes — Mathematics 35, Reasoning 35, General Awareness 50. Both are single-block tests with 1/3 negative marking, and **English is not tested**.

faqs.q: Does CBT 1 count towards the final merit?
faqs.a: CBT 1 is the screening stage for the next CBT. Read the current post-specific CEN for CBT 2 merit and the qualifying typing stage where applicable; do not import another cycle’s CBAT weighting.

faqs.q: What is CBAT and who has to take it?
faqs.a: CBAT rules apply to posts such as Station Master and Traffic Assistant in the recruitment cycles that advertise them. Neither post is listed in the current CEN 06/2026 four-post graduate table. Use your own CEN’s post mapping rather than copying another cycle’s aptitude requirements.

faqs.q: Which posts have a typing test and what speed is needed?
faqs.a: Typist posts — Senior Clerk cum Typist, Junior Account Assistant cum Typist, Junior Clerk cum Typist and Accounts Clerk cum Typist — have a qualifying typing skill test. The required speed is **30 words per minute in English or 25 in Hindi**. Marks from the typing test don't count in merit; you only have to qualify.

faqs.q: What is the age limit and the cut-off date for the 2026 cycle?
faqs.a: The current detailed tables specify 18–33 for graduate posts and 18–30 for undergraduate posts as on 1 January 2027, with the category relaxations and date-of-birth limits set out in the respective CEN.

faqs.q: What is the application fee and is any of it refunded?
faqs.a: **₹500 for General/OBC and ₹250 for SC/ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, women, transgender, minority and EBC candidates.** After you appear in CBT 1, **₹400 is refunded to the ₹500 category and the full ₹250 to the reduced-fee category**, so the effective cost is small if you actually sit the exam.

faqs.q: Can I apply to both the graduate and undergraduate CEN?
faqs.a: A graduate is generally eligible for both, since the undergraduate posts ask for Class 12 as the minimum, and the two notifications run on different application windows. Whether it's wise depends on your prep time: both use the same Maths-Reasoning-GA pattern, but the undergraduate CBT 1 is a separate exam. Read the detailed CENs for any rule on applying to more than one.

faqs.q: Which graduate post is the best in RRB NTPC?
faqs.a: In CEN 06/2026, Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor is Level 6 with initial pay ₹35,400. Goods Train Manager, Junior Accounts Assistant cum Typist and Senior Clerk cum Typist are Level 5 with initial pay ₹29,200. Compare job setting, medical conditions and any typing requirement before ordering preferences. Station Master and Traffic Assistant are not in this current graduate table.

faqs.q: Is there any interview in RRB NTPC?
faqs.a: No. Selection is through CBT 1, CBT 2, the post-specific skill test where applicable, document verification and a medical examination.

documents: Keep these ready for the application and for **Document Verification**: **Class 10 certificate** (date of birth proof), **graduation marksheets and degree** (for graduate posts) or **Class 12 marksheet** (for undergraduate posts), **category certificate** in the central-government format (OBC-NCL, EWS, SC or ST), **PwBD or ex-servicemen certificate** where applicable, **photo ID** (Aadhaar or equivalent), recent **passport photographs**, scanned **signature**, and your **linked mobile number and email ID**. Make sure the name and date of birth are spelled identically everywhere — mismatches are the commonest verification delay. OBC-NCL candidates should hold a certificate valid for the relevant financial year, or they may be considered under the unreserved category.
